scope: Named captured shell environment parameters, quote-aware field splitting and previous pipeline status; deferred argument and lexical redirect expansion in a scoped native Rust Shell handle

implementation.owner: Rust Shell owns source tokenization, word fragments, environment and expansion. Effect owns gates, authorization, native file opens, process observation and handle release on every scope exit.
implementation.bridge: Only control flow and redirection kinds cross the plan bridge. Word fragments stay in Rust; environment is decoded once per execution. The obsolete Kernel.shell_plan export and all callers were removed.
implementation.order: Arguments expand after gate selection; each redirect expands immediately before its own lexical open. Expanded values never re-enter the parser.
implementation.status: Every command in one pipeline expands the status from before that pipeline; following commands observe the final, possibly negated pipeline status.
implementation.persistence: Archived shell source and captured environment are unchanged. Native Queue tests retain the old map after config.patch and replacement Workers.
implementation.limits: 1 MiB source; 8192 parser tokens/fragments; at most 4096 resulting fields and 1 MiB of expanded bytes per argument vector or redirect word; environment uses existing 128-entry/64 KiB contract.

validation.completeCheck: Build, SDK declarations, typecheck, workspace Clippy -D warnings and Rust workspace tests passed. Final native regression: 332 tests across 54 files, 3890 assertions, 207.36 seconds.
validation.rustOracle: 117 native sh comparisons from 13 word forms and nine values; NUL-delimited oracle output verifies empty fields, spaces, tabs/newlines and Unicode. Additional Rust tests cover status, explicit unsupported syntax and quotas.
validation.native: Quotes, empty/missing values, immutable environment, skipped expansion quotas, pre-pipeline status, ordered/ambiguous redirects, stderr selection, empty command 127, denied writes, no source reparse and delayed Queue delivery across Worker replacement.
validation.consumerDelta: Final proof/fixture changes passed typecheck and five native SDK/parameter tests, 61 assertions, 4.22 seconds. Exact archives passed public export/declaration checks and native service binding/Agent RPC, including shell parameters.
validation.probeLocal: The ten-case production probe was first executed against native local Alchemy workerd/R2 through the compiled SDK and passed.
validation.scan: Source and both extracted archives passed gitleaks. Both Apache-2.0 licenses exactly match source; no env or node_modules archive entries.
validation.metadataCorrection: Metadata-only archive lookup and typed continuation logging passed build/typecheck and six native tests across four files, 141 assertions, 10.60 seconds; then the final 332-test regression and exact archived runtime consumer proof passed.

benchmark.limits: Current native workerd benchmark on a shared host. Prior report was retained before replacement, not an ABBA or controlled same-source comparison. No production latency or AgentOS cost advantage is established.

deployment.workerKind: ordinary Cloudflare Worker; no Dynamic Workers or Worker Loader
deployment.physicalResources: Existing Worker, private R2 bucket and execution Queue retained

initialAttempt.result: Worker uploaded; 45 process pages confirmed with zero changes; next page hit the client 120-second timeout
initialAttempt.persistedState: No rollback inferred; read-only native Alchemy/R2 inspection confirmed current archive markers and retained receipt state. Subsequent deployment repeated the bounded scan and converged with zero changes.

metadataPath.finding: The already-converted code path used R2 get for metadata and returned without consuming the body. Current code uses native head; only legacy conversion opens a conditional body read and consumes it. Progress logs now preserve the native page continuation.
metadataPath.confidence: The original timeout did not reproduce locally. A real native page with 25 references to a multi-MiB archive passed before and after the change; unchanged source and receipt ETags were verified. The metadata-only replay completed remotely. This does not isolate a provider/network cause or assert the old six-body connection-limit behavior.

limitations: Not a complete POSIX shell: pathname patterns, assignments, parameter operators, positional/special parameters and command substitution remain unsupported.
Shell-owned variable initialization, configurable field separators, compound statements, jobs, PTY and original stream ordering remain open.
No interpreter-state recovery or new arbitrary-crash/effect-intent boundary is added.
SDK/runtime publication and Minutei binding/model delivery remain pending; the GitHub credential collection remains locked and the public latest release is sdk-v0.9.0.
